title: Top K Frequent Elements
description: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` values that occur most often. The answer is guaranteed to be unambiguous, and you may return it in any order. Try to beat O(n log n).

examples.explanation: 3 appears three times and 2 appears twice.

constraints: 1 <= k <= number of distinct values in nums
hints: First you need how often each value occurs. Which structure gives you counts in one pass?
A frequency can never exceed n. What if you indexed an array by frequency?
Bucket values by their count (bucket i holds values appearing i times), then read buckets from the highest count down until you have k values.
starterCode:
class Solution:
    def topKFrequent(self, nums: List[int], k: int) -> List[int]:

args.$py: [i for i in range(1, 441) for _ in range(i)]

solution.explanation: Count occurrences with a hash map. A value can occur at most n times, so create n+1 buckets where bucket i lists the values with count i. Then sweep the buckets from highest count to lowest, collecting values until k have been gathered. Counting and bucketing are linear, so time is O(n) and space is O(n). A min-heap of size k gives O(n log k) as an alternative.
